provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Common entrance ICT review
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state basic ICT components.
The pupils should be able to solve practical computer tasks.

Introduction:
Today we will review what we have learned in ICT this year. This will help us prepare for our common entrance examination.

Content:
We will cover computer parts like monitor, keyboard, and mouse. We will also review software types like system software and application software. We will practice opening programs and saving files. We will discuss internet safety rules and how to search for information online.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in pairs to label computer parts and demonstrate basic computer operations.

Evaluation questions:
What are the main parts of a computer?
How do you save a document?
Why is internet safety important?

Summary:
Today we reviewed important ICT topics that will help us in our common entrance examination.

topics.title: Advanced word processing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to create tables in a document.
The pupils should be able to perform mail merge operations.

Introduction:
We have learned basic word processing before. Today we will learn more advanced features like tables and mail merge.

Content:
Tables help organize information neatly in rows and columns. Mail merge helps create personalized letters by combining a main document with a data source. For example, we can create graduation certificates with each pupil's name. We will practice making tables for timetables and lists.

Class activity:
Pupils will create a table showing their class timetable and perform a mail merge to create personalized graduation invitation cards.

Evaluation questions:
What is the purpose of tables in word processing?
What is mail merge used for?
How do you insert a table in Microsoft Word?

Summary:
Today we learned advanced word processing features that will help us create organized documents.

topics.title: Spreadsheet project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to create a budget spreadsheet.
The pupils should be able to generate charts from spreadsheet data.

Introduction:
We have learned about spreadsheets before. Today we will use them to plan a graduation budget and create charts.

Content:
A spreadsheet helps organize numbers and perform calculations. For our graduation budget, we will list expenses like decorations, food, and hall rental. We will use formulas to calculate totals and averages. Charts help visualize data clearly. We will create pie charts showing expense categories and bar charts comparing costs.

Class activity:
Pupils will create a graduation budget spreadsheet with at least five expense items, calculate totals, and create two different types of charts.

Evaluation questions:
What is a spreadsheet used for?
How do you calculate totals in a spreadsheet?
What type of chart would best show expense categories?

Summary:
Today we used spreadsheets to plan a budget and create visual charts to represent our data.

topics.title: Coding project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to plan a simple app.
The pupils should be able to write basic code for their app.

Introduction:
We have learned about coding basics before. Today we will plan and create a simple application for our graduation project.

Content:
Planning an app involves deciding what it will do and how users will interact with it. We will use flowcharts to show the steps our app will take. For coding, we will use Scratch or a similar visual programming language. We will create simple animations or games related to our school or graduation theme.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to plan their app using a flowchart and then code a simple version using Scratch.

Evaluation questions:
What is the first step in planning an app?
What is a flowchart used for?
Name one block you might use in Scratch programming.

Summary:
Today we planned and started coding our graduation project applications.

topics.title: Web basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives: The pupils should be able to explain how websites work. The pupils should be able to write simple HTML code. Introduction: We use websites every day for learning and entertainment. Today we will learn how they work and create our own simple webpage. Content: Websites are made of HTML code that tells the browser what to display. HTML uses tags like , , and to structure content. We will learn basic tags like

for headings,

for paragraphs, and for images. We will create a simple webpage about our school or graduation. Class activity: Pupils will create a simple HTML webpage about their favorite subject in school using basic HTML tags. Evaluation questions: What does HTML stand for? Name three HTML tags you can use. How do you create a heading in HTML? Summary: Today we learned how websites work and created our own simple webpage using HTML.

topics.title: Digital citizenship
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain digital etiquette and laws.
The pupils should be able to create a digital citizenship pledge.

Introduction:
When we use technology, we need to follow rules to stay safe and respectful. Today we will learn about digital citizenship.

Content:
Digital citizenship means using technology responsibly. This includes being polite online, not sharing personal information, and not copying others' work. We must follow copyright laws and not download music or movies illegally. We will discuss cyberbullying and how to report it. We will create pledges promising to be good digital citizens.

Class activity:
Pupils will create a digital citizenship poster or pledge that outlines responsible online behavior.

Evaluation questions:
What is digital citizenship?
Why should you not share personal information online?
What should you do if you see cyberbullying?

Summary:
Today we learned about responsible technology use and created pledges to be good digital citizens.

topics.title: Entrepreneurship with ICT
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify digital business opportunities.
The pupils should be able to create a simple tech service plan.

Introduction:
Technology can help us start businesses even as young students. Today we will learn about digital entrepreneurship.

Content:
Digital entrepreneurship involves using technology to provide services or sell products. Examples include tutoring online, creating educational videos, or selling crafts through social media. We will discuss how to identify what people need. We will create simple business plans for digital services we could offer, including what we need to start and how much to charge.

Class activity:
Pupils will create a one-page business plan for a digital service they could offer, such as teaching younger students computer skills.

Evaluation questions:
What is digital entrepreneurship?
Name two digital business ideas for students.
What should you include in a simple business plan?

Summary:
Today we learned how to use technology for entrepreneurship and created our own tech service plans.

topics.title: Portfolio building
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to collect their best ICT work.
The pupils should be able to organize a digital portfolio.

Introduction:
Throughout this term, we have created many ICT projects. Today we will organize them into a portfolio to showcase our learning.

Content:
A portfolio shows your best work and skills. We will select our best projects from word processing, spreadsheets, coding, and web design. We will organize them in a folder with clear labels. Each project should have a brief description of what we did and what we learned. We will also include reflections on how we improved our ICT skills.

Class activity:
Pupils will create a digital folder containing their best work with descriptions and organize it into categories.

Evaluation questions:
What is the purpose of a portfolio?
What should you include in your portfolio description?
How will organizing your portfolio help you in the future?

Summary:
Today we organized our ICT work into portfolios that showcase our skills and learning.

topics.title: Graduation presentation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to present their ICT portfolio.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate their projects effectively.

Introduction:
Today is our demo day where we will showcase all the ICT skills we have learned this year through our projects.

Content:
Presenting your portfolio involves explaining each project clearly and showing what you learned. We will practice speaking confidently about our work. We will demonstrate how our projects work, like showing how a spreadsheet calculates totals or how an app responds to user input. We will also explain how these skills can help us in future studies and careers.

Class activity:
Pupils will present their portfolios to the class, demonstrating their projects and explaining what they learned.

Evaluation questions:
What should you include when presenting your portfolio?
Why is it important to practice your presentation?
How can your ICT skills help you in the future?

Summary:
Today we presented our portfolios and demonstrated our ICT projects to showcase our learning.

topics.title: Revision and graduation project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to showcase their best ICT work.
The pupils should be able to participate in ICT awards.

Introduction:
Today we will celebrate our learning by showcasing our best work and recognizing excellence in ICT among our classmates.

Content:
For our final showcase, we will display our best projects from the term. This includes our word processing documents, spreadsheets, coding projects, and web pages. We will also create a digital exhibition of our work. For ICT awards, we will recognize pupils who showed exceptional skills, creativity, and improvement in ICT throughout the term.

Class activity:
Pupils will set up a digital exhibition of their work and participate in an awards ceremony recognizing excellence in different ICT areas.

Evaluation questions:
What project are you most proud of and why?
What ICT skill do you think will be most useful to you in the future?
How has learning ICT helped you this year?

Summary:
Today we celebrated our ICT learning through a final showcase and awards ceremony.
